name: Traefik
summary: A dynamic edge router that ingests configuration from multiple providers, builds routers, services, and middleware chains, and manages TLS certificates as routing state.

features.name: Provider-driven dynamic configuration
features.description: Traefik queries orchestrators, container engines, files, and key-value stores for routing information and updates routes when provider state changes.
costs: Provider-specific namespaces and update timing affect routing behavior

features.name: Router, service, and middleware composition
features.description: A router matches incoming traffic and connects it to a service; middleware objects can be chained to transform or control request processing before the service handler.
benefits: Separates matching, backend selection, and policy stages
costs: Ordering and cross-provider references become part of request semantics

features.name: Dynamic TLS certificate stores
features.description: TLS certificates can be added or removed through dynamic configuration, selected by SNI, and grouped in the globally available default TLS store.
benefits: Allows certificate rotation without rebuilding the proxy
costs: Certificate selection occurs before HTTP router rules and has a distinct fallback path

mathematical_views.question: How do provider observations become a coherent set of routers, services, middlewares, and TLS objects?
assumptions: Provider events are modeled as updates to typed configuration nodes
The view abstracts provider-specific watch and polling mechanisms
A route is usable only after referenced objects are available

mathematical_views.question: Which matching, middleware, service, and backend stages process a request, and in what order?
assumptions: Routers are match predicates with references to services
Middleware chains are ordered transformations or controls
The model does not infer latency or fault tolerance

mathematical_views.question: How does a TLS connection select a certificate before HTTP routing begins?
assumptions: Client SNI is the input to certificate selection
The default TLS store is the fallback when no match exists
HTTP router rules are evaluated only after TLS establishment

benefits: Automatic route updates from infrastructure state
costs: Provider heterogeneity and propagation timing complicate predictability
Ordering and references enlarge the configuration state space
SNI/TLS state is separate from later HTTP route matching
